newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C-C Amatil says no change to SanMiguel deal.
newsitem.headline: C-C Amatil says no change to SanMiguel deal.

text.p: Australian soft-drink bottler Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd said on Wednesday the Philippines' San Miguel Corp would not gain more than three seats on C-C Amatil's 12-member board following their planned tie-up.

There would also be no increase in San Miguel's proposed 25 percent holding in C-C Amatil, and the Philippine food and beverage giant would not play a role in C-C Amatil's executive management, a C-C Amatil spokesman said.

San Miguel on Tuesday won shareholder approval for a deal under which C-C Amatil will acquire San Miguel's 70 percent stake in Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc in exchange for a 25 percent shareholding in C-C Amatil.
However, reservations about the agreement were expressed at the meeting, which was broadcast live on state television.
Magtanggol Gunigundo, chairman of the Presidential Commission on Good Government, which holds nearly half of San Miguel's shares, called for increased representation on C-C Amatil's board.
Gunigundo was also reported as saying a San Miguel representative should serve as C-C Amatil's treasurer or comptroller, and that San Miguel should have received more than 25 percent of C-C Amatil.
"Obviously there will be some fine tuning, but the basic structure of the deal ... in terms of those three things is solid," a C-C Amatil spokesman told Reuters.
He said San Miguel had advised C-C Amatil that it had told shareholders that the essential terms of the deal could not be renegotiated.
Under the agreement announced on April 4, the Australian bottler will issue 293 million shares to acquire the Philippines soft drink unit, including the 30 percent owned by the The Coca Cola Co.
The deal has led to a fall in San Miguel's share price on fears that it is losing one of its better performing units.
